speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Income Tax (Amendment No 3) Bill of 2016, or "the Bill" in short, covers income tax changes announced in the 2016 Budget Statement, an amendment to implement country-by-country reporting, as well as other changes arising from the periodic review of our income tax regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We sought views from the public on the draft Bill from 8 July to 29 July 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MOF has evaluated all the feedback received and, where relevant, accepted the suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These changes seek to transform our economy through enterprise and innovation, as well as to build a more caring and resilient society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will provide greater support to help all qualifying companies, especially SMEs, to address immediate concerns, while encouraging restructuring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clause 51 of the Bill provides for the change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Companies can, therefore, enjoy a maximum tax allowance of $10 million on their qualifying share acquisitions, up from $5 million.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clauses 23 and 63 of the Bill provide for the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, to provide upfront certainty to companies for their corporate restructuring, the non-taxation of companies' gains on disposal of their equity investments has been extended until 31 May 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clause 11 of the Bill provides for the change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fourth, to support firms, especially SMEs, to seek new markets and new growth opportunities overseas, the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation scheme has been extended till 31 March 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clauses 13 and 14 of the Bill provide for the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This change will take effect from Year of Assessment 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clauses 25 to 28 of the Bill provide for the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Sixth, to encourage volunteerism among businesses, a pilot Business and Institutions of Public Character (IPCs) Partnership Scheme was introduced from 1 July 2016 till end 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Businesses that organise their employees to volunteer and provide services to IPCs, including secondments, will receive a total of 250% tax deduction on qualifying expenditure incurred, subject to the receiving IPC's agreement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The qualifying expenditure will be subject to a yearly cap of $250,000 per business and $50,000 per IPC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clauses 17 and 18 of the Bill provide for the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a BEPS associate, Singapore has committed to Page: 15 implementing country-by-country reporting, a minimum standard under the G20/OECD action plan to counter BEPS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore-headquartered multinational enterprise groups with global consolidated revenues exceeding $1.125 billion will be required to submit to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) an annual report containing the income, taxes paid and other indicators of their level of economic activities in every tax jurisdiction where they operate, from their financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IRAS will then exchange the reports bilaterally with jurisdictions with whom Singapore has concluded Competent Authority Agreements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clauses 53, 54, 55, 56 and 58 of the Bill provide for the implementation of country-by-country reporting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I shall now outline two other key changes arising from MOF's periodic review of the tax regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, we will delink the income tax relief limit for CPF cash top-ups from the CPF top-up limit from 1 January 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The CPF top-up limit to the Retirement Account has been raised from the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) to the Enhanced Retirement Sum which is 1.5 times of the FRS, from 1 January 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To keep tax benefits focused on supporting basic retirement needs, the limit on tax relief for cash top-ups will be maintained at the FRS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clause 24 of the Bill provides for the change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, we will grant tax deduction of up to 200% for qualifying expenditure incurred on qualifying retail bonds issued from 19 May 2016 to 18 May 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Such qualifying expenditure include professional fees, origination, underwriting and distribution fees, as well as advertising and marketing expenses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will further encourage the issuance of retail bonds and broaden the range of investment options available to retail investors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Clauses 16 and 18 of the Bill provide for the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The remaining legislative changes are mostly technical in nature or relate to improvements in tax administration.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I welcome these progressive and timely amendments to the Income Tax Act, which support domestic businesses and spur economic growth, especially in view of the forecasted sluggish growth in 2017.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In its twice-yearly Macroeconomic Review released on 25 October 2016, MAS stated that global growth is expected to come in at 3.7% this year and edge up slightly to 3.8% next year, as business investments in major economies stay sluggish due to the elevated economic uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The central bank also said that business sentiment remains negative, especially among small and medium-sized enterprises.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a nation, we have to face the upcoming tough challenges together in the year ahead.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, it is encouraging that Government policy continues to be relevant to meet the needs of the finance sector and other businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Page: 16 Here, let me highlight two aspects of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As the Senior Minister of State had mentioned, Corporate Income Tax Rebate is given to all companies to help them with rising business costs and is applicable for Years of Assessment 2013 to 2017.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For Years of Assessment 2013 to 2015, companies received 30% income tax rebate, capped at $30,000.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For Years of Assessment 2016 to 2017, companies were to receive 30%, capped at $20,000.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The cap reduced the maximum rebate by $10,000 from what it was previously.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I welcome this change as this is in line with the Government's direction for more effective delivery of public service.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is also in line with the Government's Smart Nation vision to harness technology to enhance productivity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While I commend our move to lead a life more empowered by technology, this may be difficult for some of the staff members, particularly those in the older generation, who may be unfamiliar with such computer systems.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This may impede their productivity, or even cause them to be replaced by businesses if they are unable to rise to the task.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, I would suggest that the phasing out be taken at a slower pace, especially for traditional businesses, which should have the option of opting-out of mandatory e-filing with good reasons.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is also as we have seen an increase in the number of retrenchments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: IRAS can consider these applications on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration the age and capabilities of administrative staff members of the company.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These comments notwithstanding, Madam, this Bill can only serve the interests of Singapore's businesses and economy, and I stand in support of it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With regard to Mr Louis Ng's query on the rationale behind the reduction of the Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rebate quantum cap by $10,000, it may be helpful if I explain the circumstances.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In Budget 2015, the CIT rebate was further extended for another two years, that is, for YAs 2016 and 2017, at the same rate of 30% of tax payable, but up to a lower cap of $20,000 per Year of Assessment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The intent was to continue to support firms in the period of restructuring, while Page: 17 phasing out the support gradually.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I note Mr Louis Ng's concern on the current economic climate.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the intent was to address the immediate concerns while encouraging companies, especially the SMEs, to restructure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The cap remains at $20,000 per Year of Assessment to ensure the focus remains on SMEs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Apart from the CIT rebate, however, businesses can also benefit from other grant schemes, for example, the Wage Credit Scheme and the Capability Development Grant, which are targeted at smaller businesses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will continue to monitor closely the economic outlook and consider further business assistance measures if necessary.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With regard to electronic filing, we agree with Mr Louis Ng on the need to consider the difficulties that may be faced by small and traditional businesses with the introduction of mandatory electronic-filing or "e-filing" for corporate income tax returns.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To assist companies, especially small and traditional ones, the mandatory e-filing will be introduced in a phased approach as follows.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We would also like to assure Mr Louis Ng that IRAS will help companies transit to e-filing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, IRAS will be holding e-filing workshops for SMEs and tax agents where participants can experience e-filing using a demonstration kit.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, there is a hotline available to answer questions regarding e-filing services.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Third, SMEs can visit the IRAS taxpayer service centre for one-to-one assistance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Fourth, IRAS will also reach out to taxpayers to provide assistance where necessary for the companies to e-file.      .
